learningObjectives.title: Threats to networks (malware, phishing, social engineering)

questions.q: In a star network topology, how are the client devices connected?
options: Each device connects to a central switch or hub
Each device connects directly to every other device
All devices are connected along a single backbone cable
Devices are connected in a closed loop
questions.explain: In a star topology every device has its own cable connecting it to a central switch or hub.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a full mesh topology?
options: Every device is directly connected to every other device
All devices connect to one central switch
All devices share a single central cable
Devices are arranged in a single ring
questions.explain: In a full mesh, each node has a direct connection to every other node, giving multiple routes for data.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of a star topology?
options: If one cable fails, only the device on that cable is affected
It requires no central switch, reducing cost
Every device has a direct link to every other device
Adding a new device slows down all existing devices
questions.explain: Because each device has its own dedicated cable to the switch, a single cable fault only isolates that one device.

questions.q: Why is a mesh topology considered highly reliable?
options: There are multiple routes for data, so there is no single point of failure
It uses the least amount of cabling of any topology
All data must pass through one central device
It cannot be affected by network congestion
questions.explain: Multiple redundant paths mean data can be rerouted if one connection fails, avoiding a single point of failure.

questions.q: What does HTTPS provide that HTTP does not?
options: Encryption of data sent between the browser and the web server
Faster transfer of files over the internet
The ability to send emails between servers
Compression of web pages to save bandwidth
questions.explain: HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP, encrypting communication between the browser and server.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to send email from a client to a mail server?
options: SMTP
FTP
HTTP
IMAP
questions.explain: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending email.

questions.q: In the TCP/IP protocol stack, what is the main role of IP?
options: Addressing and routing packets to the correct destination
Splitting data into packets and reassembling them in order
Encrypting the contents of each packet
Displaying web pages in the browser
questions.explain: IP (Internet Protocol) handles the addressing and routing of packets, while TCP handles splitting and reassembly.

questions.q: Why is the TCP/IP model divided into layers?
options: Each layer is self-contained, so one layer can be changed without affecting the others
It makes the network run faster by removing protocols
It prevents any encryption from being used
It allows only one manufacturer's hardware to be used
questions.explain: Layering makes protocols self-contained so a change in one layer does not affect the others, aiding development and maintenance.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes phishing?
options: Sending fraudulent emails or messages that appear genuine to trick users into revealing personal information
Flooding a server with requests so it cannot respond
Software that secretly records the keys a user presses
Trying every possible password until the correct one is found
questions.explain: Phishing uses fake but convincing emails or messages to trick users into handing over sensitive data.

questions.q: What is social engineering?
options: Manipulating or deceiving people into giving away confidential information or access
A method of encrypting data on a network
A type of network cable used in star topologies
Software that automatically updates a computer's operating system
questions.explain: Social engineering exploits human behaviour, tricking people rather than attacking technology directly.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a computer worm and a virus?
options: A worm can self-replicate and spread without attaching to a file, whereas a virus attaches to a host file
A virus can spread across networks but a worm cannot
A worm only affects hardware, while a virus only affects software
A virus cannot be removed by anti-malware but a worm can
questions.explain: Worms self-replicate and spread independently, while viruses attach to a host file and usually need user action to spread.

questions.q: What does ransomware typically do?
options: Encrypts a user's files and demands payment to unlock them
Secretly records keystrokes and sends them to an attacker
Disguises itself as a legitimate program to gain access
Overloads a server with traffic to take it offline
questions.explain: Ransomware encrypts the victim's data and demands a ransom for the decryption key.

questions.q: Which type of malware is disguised as legitimate software to trick a user into installing it?
options: A Trojan
A worm
Spyware
A denial of service attack
questions.explain: A Trojan appears to be a genuine, useful program but carries a harmful payload.

questions.q: How does a denial of service (DoS) attack disrupt a network?
options: It floods a server with so many requests that it cannot respond to legitimate users
It encrypts all the files stored on the server
It steals passwords by intercepting network traffic
It tricks users into revealing their login details
questions.explain: A DoS attack overwhelms a server with requests so genuine users cannot access the service.

questions.q: How does an SQL injection attack work?
options: Malicious SQL code is entered into an input box to gain access to or manipulate a database
The attacker floods a website with fake user accounts
A virus rewrites the SQL software on the server
The attacker guesses the administrator's password repeatedly
questions.explain: SQL injection enters malicious SQL commands through input fields to access or alter a poorly secured database.

questions.q: An attacker uses software that automatically tries thousands of different password combinations to log into an account. What is this an example of?
options: A brute force attack
A phishing attack
A Trojan
Data interception
questions.explain: A brute force attack systematically tries many password combinations until the correct one is found.

questions.q: A school wants to monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic, blocking unauthorised connections based on a set of rules. Which security measure should it use?
options: A firewall
A penetration test
Encryption
Anti-virus software
questions.explain: A firewall inspects traffic against rules and blocks unauthorised incoming or outgoing connections.

questions.q: What is the purpose of penetration testing?
options: To deliberately probe a network for vulnerabilities before real attackers can exploit them
To encrypt all data stored on a network
To back up important files automatically
To block spam emails from reaching users
questions.explain: Penetration testing simulates attacks to find and fix weaknesses before genuine attackers exploit them.

questions.q: A company sends sensitive customer data across a network and wants it to be unreadable to anyone who intercepts it. Which measure achieves this?
options: Encryption
A firewall
User access levels
Penetration testing
questions.explain: Encryption scrambles data so that intercepted information is meaningless without the decryption key.

questions.q: In a hospital system, nurses can view patient records but only doctors can edit them. Which security measure is being used?
options: User access levels
A firewall
Anti-malware software
A brute force attack
questions.explain: User access levels restrict what each user can see or do, limiting access to only what their role requires.
